While scrolling through social media on Mike's phone, Alex discovered that Rachel had booked a pricey room at an upscale restaurant, planning some "intimate" celebration of her own – with no guests from their group, naturally.

Alex didn't want to give up yet; he tried dialing Rachel, but Mike picked up, blowing off the whole thing. It turned out he'd been too distracted by his new gaming console delivery to even notice it was someone's birthday that day. Feeling hollow and useless, Alex retreated behind a wall of calm determination.

Now, he rummaged through his bag for some more bunting he could bring to Mike's party – but why had Rachel decided not to include their friend group? His heart sank as the realization crept in like water slowly seeping into tiny cracks. Now every so often, another guest would text asking about confirmation or details – but whenever Amelia called Rachel's number, it went straight to voicemail. Amelia thought she was starting to get the message, but something inside her refused to give up without making one final attempt. Her eyes scanned the garden behind the house – what if this rainy evening could suddenly transform into a perfect night for their little group?

"Rachel sent me," someone just called out from behind the hedge, accompanied by a hesitant knock on the door in rhythm with her thundering heartbeat.

Alex rubbed his temples. They owed him an explanation after just going ahead with this massive birthday bash against his expectations. "She could've, like... decided we needed a day alone," Emily ventured, but Alex didn't find it reassuring enough. Her friend had to see the look of growing panic in his eyes – every so often Rachel seemed to do something that turned what everyone else thought they'd planned inside out.

Why did Jamie always have to go first? Why couldn't he just let me have my moment this once? "So, what's all the hubbub about?" a fellow classmate called out as they nodded hello. My voice came out tight and clipped in response: "Just celebrating Sarah... again."

We stood awkwardly for a beat before they excused themselves. It only made sense that no one would join me once Jamie's louder party was the talk of town. As I sulked through the rest of my day, my fists curled up into fists.

Later that night, Jaden was no match for Olivia's radiant after-party atmosphere when they began to reminisce over the day's bittersweet moments and laughter. All it took was catching a glimpse of how unimpressed Alex looked in his suit – surrounded by admirers but awkwardly unable to participate – for their unease finally erupting into full-blown silence, a cold, dark shadow spreading from my head down through every fiber of my being.
